sections.h2: Land is not what is missing: mapped parks already have 1.35 lakh hectares available

chart.title: BHAVYA's 0.14 lakh hectares is about 10% of the land already available

sections.means: The government's own land bank lists 1.35 lakh hectares available, so the scheme's case rests on quality rather than quantity.
sections.todo: Publish occupancy of mapped parks over time so BHAVYA parks can be judged on how fast they fill.

sections.h2: Proposals only partly follow the biggest unbuilt investment backlogs

chart.title: Karnataka and Odisha hold the second and third largest unbuilt investment backlogs
chart.sub: Filed but unbuilt factory investment, 2020-25, Rs crore. Proposal counts are in the text below.
chart.source: DPIIT IEM filings, as analysed in this blog; BHAVYA round-one proposals.

sections.means: Maharashtra leads both lists, but Karnataka and Odisha, with large unbuilt backlogs, sent five or fewer proposals each.
sections.todo: Score proposals on connectivity, site suitability and industrial ecosystem, so that demand from industry counts more than proposal numbers.

sections.h2: Earlier zones filled slowly: 95 of 372 notified SEZs were not operating

chart.title: 95 of 372 notified SEZs were not operating on 31 July 2026
chart.source: Figures as reported in this post, 31 July 2026.

sections.means: The post's SEZ count shows that earlier zones were approved faster than they were filled.
sections.todo: Judge BHAVYA parks on land allotted, investment and production rather than approvals, as the Finance Minister urged in August.
